title.narrative: Multisectoral Assistance to IDPs and Host Communities Affected by Conflict in Northwest and Southern Tigray and Amhara

description.narrative: The primary objective is to improve living conditions and the dignity of crisis-affected populations in Northwest and Southern Tigray through better access to essential household items, adequate shelter, protection, and vital basic services. IOM will implement both the SNFI and CCCM through direct implementation and implementing partners. 446 households (2,230 individuals) will be reached through IOM direct implementation, and the remaining will be reached through implementing partners in Southern and Northwest Tigray through shelter repair and reconstruction, providing a combination of in-kind assistance and cash support. In addition to shelter support, beneficiaries will receive tailored housing, land, and property (HLP) assistance, including information provision, verification of tenure Security Documents (TSD) and technical guidance on specific HLP issues. The project will also conduct capacity-building sessions to promote awareness of HLP rights among government counterparts and stakeholders. IOM will ensure that all households targeted to receive shelter assistance, relevant local authorities, and community leaders receive adequate information and capacity building on HLP rights and that the appropriate due diligence is done to mitigate HLP-related risks. IOM will assess household needs and create a tailored Bill of Quantity (BOQ) for shelter support, adjusting material distribution per household. Cash assistance will be provided for labor and local materials, stimulating the economy. Engineers will train carpenters, monitor construction, and offer guidance to ensure quality and effective use of materials. To further strengthen community resilience, through direct implementation, IOM will expand its Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) operations in the Northwest areas by establishing one community resource center. In this and additional community resource centers (to be established by partners, per below), IOM will facilitate service mapping, site planning, community engagement, and implementing complaints and feedback mechanisms for 42,826 beneficiaries, ensuring that protection considerations are integrated throughout the CM response. IOM through local partners in Tigray to address critical gaps in assistance through two key components: CCCM, and shelter and non-food item (NFI) support through sector-specific, unconditional cash assistance. Three community resource centers will be established in the woredas of Alamata (10,103 individuals), Korem (5,613 individuals) in Southern Tigray, and Aminata/Kobo Warada (6,735 individuals) in Amhara, serving as multisectoral hubs for both Returnees and host communities with estimated reach of 22,450 individuals in the targeted area; 15,715 out of them are returnees. These centers will provide essential services and resources to meet immediate needs. The centers serve as hubs for service mapping, site planning, and community engagement activities. Additionally, the Rapid Response Fund (RRF) Partners will distribute 500 NFI kits to support returnees and deliver unconditional cash assistance in the southern region for 1,114 households (USD 115 per HH), enabling beneficiaries to address urgent shelter and needs of essential household items, with an estimated reach of 70% returnees and 30% host community members.
